thesis: Claims about Allah made without knowledge are grave fabrications, and even when such lies yield brief worldly enjoyment they never amount to real success (falah) before Allah.
notes: Carried by all four editions. sultan = hujjah verified; 25/25 morphology comments verify. Interfaith adab: file keeps the walad claim abstract, never names communities — avoids polemic. No absolute claims fail.

thesis: The verse's unnamed passive commands show a cosmos that obeys Allah instantly and totally, with the decree completing on schedule and only persistent wrongdoing finally cast away.

flags.quote: This is one of the verses the Arabic rhetorical tradition has returned to again and again as a summit of the Qur'an's eloquence. That reputation is not sentiment.
flags.issue: None of the four fetched editions discuss the verse's balaghah reputation. Consistent with wider rhetoric literature (proverbial ijaz) but asserted as fact and unverifiable in-pipeline — the claim class the rubric flags rather than trusts.

flags.quote: Al-Tabari traces the word back to ordinary Arabic usage for gulping something down — swallowing a thing whole, the way you swallow food.
flags.issue: The food-specificity comes from the modern editor's footnote (Ibn al-Qatta'), not al-Tabari's own text. Slightly over-attributed, substantively harmless.

notes: Everything else verifies remarkably cleanly: exactly 4 passive verbs confirmed, 7 verbs total, wa-qila frame, Tabari AND Muyassar literally open with the same three words. Fix: hedge the reputation sentence or cite outside the four-edition pipeline (Ibn Abi al-Isba' / al-Suyuti). Reviewer recommendation: soften rather than delete — the reputation is real in the wider tradition.
